newsitem.title: USA: Dow slips slowly to new session lows.
newsitem.headline: Dow slips slowly to new session lows.

text.p: The Dow Industrials slid further in afternoon trading, as selling pushed the blue chip average down 152 points to a fresh session low of 7788.
That wiped nearly two percent off the average, bringing it to a level not seen since early July.
Analysts said the selling was caused by growing fears in the stock market that the ferocious bullish atmosphere might be winding down.

Blue chips suffered worse than smaller stocks. Although the Nasdaq Composite was down 16 to 1571, its losses were only about one percent, half the Dow's. The Russell 2000 Index of small cap stocks was off two to 409, with losses of only 0.6 percent.
The Standard & Poor's 500 Index, however, had 1.6 percent of its value knocked off, shedding about 15 points to 910.

"There have been enough little signs that the economy is not really slowing down -- that is getting bonds antsy about interest rates, and that translates into worrying about stock prices," said William Cheney, chief economist for John Hancock.
The long bond was down 7/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
